subject: armadillo
pitch: A nine-banded armadillo trotting along. A shell of overlapping banded plates in dusty pinkish-tan, a pointy snout, tall leathery ears, small beady eyes, sturdy clawed feet and a long armoured tail tapering to a point. A sprinkle of coarse pale hairs pokes out between the bands.
reasoning:
I'm working out realistic proportions for a nine-banded armadillo model—body length, tail length, and shoulder height—to use as reference dimensions in the TypeScript module I'm building with the SDK.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy: a hips root joint, a spine chain curving from hips through to the neck using a catmull path, trying to figure out how joint counts map to path segments and parenting relationships for the body tube geometry.

I'm continuing to plan out the rig — adding a head joint oriented slightly downward and forward from the spine tip, a tapering tail chain hanging off the hips with a radius function that shrinks toward the tip, and now starting to sketch the leg chains for the shoulders and front limbs.

Working out leg bend directions...

So the bend direction depends on the middle joint: elbow back for front legs, knee forward for hind legs. I'm working out limb segment lengths—shoulder to elbow, elbow to wrist, wrist to toe—and deciding to simplify to two segments with the target at the foot.

Checking reachability: with the body sitting around y=0.3 and legs totaling 0.26 in length, the vertical distance to the foot wasn't actually reachable, so I'm lowering the body center to y=0.26 with leg segments 0.13 and 0.12, giving enough reach to the foot near y=0.03.

For the leg chain itself, I'm defining three points (shoulder, elbow, hand) which yields two span joints plus a tip joint, parented to a spine joint near the hips — the exact parent just affects skinning, not position. Since the body tube radius is about 0.14, placing the shoulder points at x=±0.1 keeps them properly inside the body for a clean connection.

Now I'm working out the body sweep: it follows the spine chain with a radius profile that's wider in the middle and tapers toward the head and rump, to get that armadillo shell shape. I'm setting up the radius function to vary rx/ry along the path, with the spine running from the rump around z=-0.25 to the shoulders near z=0.12.

Next I'm thinking through the shell pattern using banded stripes running as rings across the back, mimicking the nine-banded armadillo's plated segments.

Still shaping the head geometry...

Still shaping the head geometry...

Now I'm placing small beady dark eyes on the head using local coordinates with left/right mirroring via a sign multiplier, then moving on to sketch tall leathery ears via extrusion.

Still shaping ear geometry...

Now thinking through foot claws—small cone spikes for the toes, computing claw base positions from the foot tip joint so they angle forward-down naturally.

For attaching feet, I should anchor to the actual tip joint of each leg chain rather than guessing coordinates. For the tail, I'll sweep along the tail chain with a radius that tapers from wide at the base to a pointed tip, shaded with the shell color to match banding.

For texture, I'm adding scattered coarse hairs across the body surface using small spike primitives anchored at surface hit points, oriented along the surface normal with a short length and thin radius — roughly sixty of these scattered with minimum spacing for a natural, uneven distribution.

For coloring, I'm building the shell as stripes layered with a countershading paint, giving darker stripe bands along the body axis and a lighter belly tone where the surface faces downward. Legs get a darker tan, ears a leathery pink, and the snout a soft pink tone — considering whether to layer in an additional banded plate texture for extra detail.

Now I'm working out the trotting gait, figuring diagonal leg pairs moving together (front-left with hind-right forward, front-right with hind-left back), and calculating hip and foot z-coordinates for each limb to get a natural alternating stride.

Working through diagonal pairing: FL moves forward with HR, while FR and HL move back, keeping each foot's vertical reach just within the 0.25 leg-length limit so the trot stays mechanically valid.

I'm raising the hip height slightly to avoid nearly-straight, ugly legs, adjusting body radius and vertical leg span so there's a bit more natural bend while keeping the trot stylized. I'm also pinning down the hind hip socket coordinates and starting to lay out the spine path as a smooth curve between joints.

Now I'm defining the neck and head joint positions, aiming the head bone forward and slightly down, and sizing a capsule shape to represent the head attached to that bone, then placing a snout spike at its base.

Next I'm figuring out ear placement using local coordinates relative to the head joint, setting up an extrusion with left/up offsets and thickness for small ear shapes.

Now I'm positioning the eyes similarly, computing local offsets from the head joint so they sit on the sides of the head capsule near the front, checking the radius stays within the head's surface.

That's fine for the head shape — I'll keep it plain shell-colored rather than adding stripes, and go with a pinkish-tan tone for the body and head, picking a shell color like a muted tan-brown.

I'm setting up the full color palette: dusty pinkish-tan shell, darker shell shade, lighter belly tone, leg brown, dark claws and eyes, a softer pink for the ears, and a pale hair color. Then I'm defining the tail as a tapering swept shape using the shell color, narrowing toward the tip with a pointed end cap, starting from around the hip area.

I'm laying out the tail as a chain of three joints following a curved path from the hips backward, then working on the body sweep — a tube-like dome shape using sine-based width and height variation to mimic an armadillo's rounded shell, sharing the same chain and color as the spine.

For the shell texture I'm sticking with banded stripes to suggest overlapping plates rather than adding extra bumps, keeping the poly budget low. Now I'm defining the legs — two-segment limbs with a single bend each, elbows bending backward on the front legs and knees bending forward on the hind legs.

I'm now computing foot placement coordinates for each leg, checking that the horizontal and vertical distances from hip to foot stay within the leg's total reach so the limbs don't overextend.

For the trot gait, I'm confirming diagonal pairs move together—FL and HR step forward while FR and HL step back—then I start drafting a helper function to construct each leg from its hip position, foot position, and bend direction. Writing leg helper function...

Now I need to figure out the correct parent joint for each limb—whether hind legs attach to the first spine joint and front legs to a later one, based on where each spine segment actually sits along the body.

Checking the gap coverage with the round cap: body end reaches roughly z 0.22 at y 0.3, and the head capsule spans 0.14 to 0.24, so they bridge reasonably well. I should set the spine end at 0 to keep things aligned.

I'm also deciding on shell stripe spacing (roughly 4cm bands for a nine-banded armadillo look), confirming the catmull spine sweep stays smooth through its three points, and planning hair placement by scattering spike hits across the body surface, filtering out underside points, and attaching small cone-shaped hairs along each hit's normal direction.

Now I'm placing the leg and foot geometry—feet as small boxes at ground level in the leg color, with claws built as short spike cones angled forward-down from the toe base to tip, spaced across three positions per foot.

Positioning the foot box at the joint with a fixed offset point should work fine since boxes use world alignment by default.

For the legs, I'm considering using a capsule-based sweep with a tapering radius function across the three-joint chain, which naturally gives rounded caps at both ends including the foot tip. This keeps the legs looking sturdy while following the joint path smoothly.

For the snout, I'm shaping it as a long pointed spike emerging from the head capsule, with the base tucked inside the head and the visible tip tapering outward—skipping a separate shell piece for now and adding a bit of tail detail before setting up the export metadata.

Now I'm setting up imports from the builder library, pulling in utilities like rng, limb, catmull, stripes, and countershade, and working out the typing for limb chains and ear outlines so the extrude function can properly render sharp corners.

Defining ear geometry points...

Defining more color constants...

Now I'm setting up the armadillo build with hip joint positioning and a striped, countershaded shell pattern.

Defining spine chain and body sweep...

I'll leave the section option default and move to defining the head joint, using the spine's second joint as parent and aiming it forward and up. Then I'm adding a capsule shape for the head, checking the capsule function's parameter order for start/end points, radius, and bone binding.

Adding the shelled head coloring, then a spike for the snout colored with the ear tone, followed by extruding a curved outline for each ear mirrored on both sides, attached to the head bone with proper local offsets and orientation vectors.

Checking the ear placement against the head capsule's top boundary to make sure they overlap sensibly rather than floating. Then placing small sphere eyes mirrored left and right, positioned relative to the head joint.

Now I'm building out the leg-building helper function with a proper V type alias for coordinate triples and a Joint type for parent references, then wiring up the limb geometry and chain creation for each leg using hip, foot, and bend points.

Naming the joints: hip sits at the start of the hip-to-knee span, knee at the start of the knee-to-foot span, and foot is the final tip joint.

Now I'm checking whether the hip cap position overlaps with the body geometry, since the hip at x=0.1 with a 0.05 sweep radius might intersect the torso's half-width near the front end.

For the foot, I'm adding a small box for the toe pad and three claw spikes positioned along its front edge, making sure the spike bases sit within the foot box's bounds and their tips extend slightly below and forward.

Checking the round cap at the foot joint: with radius 0.038, it extends to y≈-0.013, so it sinks about 1.3cm below ground — small enough relative to overall height to be negligible.

Adjusting the sweep so the radius tapers from 0.05 to 0.03 at the end keeps the cap sinking only about 0.005, which is fine since the foot box covers it.

Now I'm defining the four leg calls (front-left, front-right, hind-left) with their hip/knee/foot joint positions and bend directions, making sure joint names stay unique per limb.

Finishing the hind-right leg call, then checking the foot placements relative to the hip — hind-right foot sits forward of its hip while hind-left sits back, which matches the body proportions I set for the front limbs too.

Next I'm building the tail as a chain of joints following a curved spline from the hip down to a tapered point tip, sweeping the radius down to a sharp "point" cap for a natural taper, and planning paint stripes as bands around it.

Now I'm scattering hair spikes across the body surface, using a random generator to place about 70 small cone spikes with minimum spacing and a filter to avoid placing them on the underside of the body.

I'm double-checking the final script for type correctness, unused variables, parent-joint references, and making sure the feet and claws rest exactly at ground level — everything looks consistent, so I'll write up the final code block with minimal extra commentary.
